answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by periodically publishing a cryptographic commitment to a unique hardware-derived entropy source that is costly to virtualize. Attackers spinning up many fake identities must buy or emulate distinct physical modules for each, since the commitment binds to non-clonable device keys. This builds a durable meadow of verified activity visible out to the horizon, while reuse of the same module is detectable on the public mesa of attestations, so capital and operational costs grow linearly with the attack size.
